title: 15.5 Event-Based Spatially Zooming Neural Interface IC with 10nW/Input Reconfigurable-Inverter Fabric and Input-Adaptive Quantization
problem: Large-scale neural interface ICs require million+ electrodes for brain interfaces, but face two bottlenecks: neural ADC power dissipation (>50× higher than 10nW/input target) and output data rate (200Gb/s required for 1M electrodes at 8b/25kHz).
motivation: Next-generation brain interfaces targeting cognitive/memory research require million-electrode density; achieving tissue-safe 10mW power budget demands ultra-low-power (10nW/input) ADCs and efficient data encoding.
method: The system exploits sparse, intermittent neural firing to hit the 10nW-per-input power target. It uses event-driven activation (reading only during spikes) and spatially-selective zooming (focusing on active electrode clusters), paired with an ultra-low-power analog-to-digital converter (ADC) using a reconfigurable-inverter fabric. Each electrode also adaptively compresses its signal (input-adaptive quantization), using fewer bits for less-informative channels, which reduces data rates and power while preserving critical neural information.
key_novelty: The innovation combines input-adaptive quantization (varying precision per electrode) with spatially-selective event-based recording (capturing only from active regions during spikes) to achieve 10nW-per-input power consumption while preserving neural information.
contributions: Avoids information loss from static electrode selection
